<p class="name">Joris Klingen</p>
<p class="role">Economist at CPB Netherlands Bureau for Economic Policy Analysis</p>
:::

<img src="images/joris.png" class="portrait" alt="Portrait of Joris Klingen">
:::

I'm an empirical economist working on how people travel and how they use energy.
At CPB, I study household energy use and the effects of green technologies such as solar panels and electric vehicles.

Much of my research uses large datasets, like bike-share trips, taxi rides and even chess games, to answer questions about transport, safety, energy consumption and the environment.
See [Research](research.qmd) for papers and work in progress.

I hold a PhD from [Spatial Economics](https://spatialeconomics.nl/) at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, supervised by Jos van Ommeren and Erik Verhoef.
I studied at [Tinbergen Institute](https://www.tinbergen.nl), VU Amsterdam and University of Amsterdam, and visited Dan Graham at Imperial College London's [Transport Strategy Centre](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/transport-engineering/transport-strategy-centre/) in 2019.

I'm also a musician: I play keys in [Flamingo Hitmix](https://flamingohitmix.com) and drums in [Bovenburen](https://bovenburen.com), and I like to develop software that is used in these music projects (see [Music](music.qmd)).
